;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[American-led intervention in Iraq (2014–2021)]]
**The [[United States Air Force]] launches a small [[shock and awe]] bombing raid using [[Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II|F-35]] and [[McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle|F-15 Eagle]] warplanes on the [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]]-occupied Qanus Island in [[Iraq]]'s [[Saladin Governorate]], dropping 36,000 kg of explosives. The small island was being used by ISIL as a "major transit hub", according to the [[Combined Joint Task Force – Operation Inherent Resolve|U.S.-led coalition]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/middle-east/isis-iraq-us-air-force-bombing-qanus-island-video-a9100526.html (''The Independent'')] [https://news.sky.com/story/is-infested-island-wiped-out-by-40-tonnes-of-explosives-11806797 (Sky News)]

;Business  and  economy
*[[Jack Ma]]  retires  and [[Daniel Zhang]]  succeeds  him as  executive chairman of  [[Alibaba Group]].  [https://www.ibtimes.com/jack-ma-retires-alibaba-everything-know-about-new-chairman-daniel-zhang-2824593 (''International Business Times'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Karbala stampede]] 
**Thirty-one pilgrims  are  killed  and  100 others  are  injured  in a [[stampede]] in  the city  of  [[Karbala]], [[Iraq]], while  marking [[Ashura]]. [https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/karbala-stampede-results-in-many-deaths-1.1568123543822 (''Gulf News'')]

;Health and environment
*[[Fukushima disaster cleanup]]
**As [[Tokyo Electric Power Company|Tepco]] says  that, by  2022, it will run out of storage room for what is now more than 1 million tonnes of [[Radioactive contamination|radioactively contaminated]] [[Nuclear reactor core|reactor core]] [[Water cooling|cooling water]], [[Minister of the Environment (Japan)|Japanese Minister of the Environment]] [[Yoshiaki Harada]] opines that "the only option will  be to [[Radiation effects from the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster|drain it  into the sea]] and dilute it". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-japan-fukushima-water-idUSKCN1VV0CC (Reuters)]

;International relations
*[[Colombia–Venezuela relations]]
**150,000 Venezuelan troops begin exercises along the Colombian border. [[Nicolás Maduro]]'s Venezuelan government says it is to intercept an attack from the other country, despite no indications there will be one. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-politics/venezuelan-military-conducts-drills-on-colombian-border-to-intercept-invasion-idUSKCN1VV2HY (Reuters)]
*[[2019 Hong Kong protests]], [[Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act]]
**[[Chief Executive of Hong Kong]] [[Carrie Lam]] urges "foreign parliaments" not to interfere in [[Hong Kong]]'s internal affairs and says continued violence "cannot solve the issues". [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/09/10/asia/carrie-lam-hong-kong-us-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]

;Politics and elections
*[[List of Trump administration dismissals and resignations]]
**[[National Security Advisor (United States)|United States National Security Advisor]] [[John R. Bolton]] is dismissed by [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]], citing strong disagreements. Bolton insists he resigned. The interim replacement is to be [[Deputy National Security Advisor (United States)|Deputy]] [[Charles Kupperman]], says the [[White House]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-49655279 (BBC News)] 
*[[September 2019 Israeli legislative election]],  [[Proposed Israeli annexation of the Jordan Valley]]
**With next week's election in sight, [[Prime Minister of Israel]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] proposes to [[Annexation|annex]] parts of the [[West Bank]] and the [[Jordan Valley]]. [[Prime Minister of the State of Palestine]] [[Mohammad Shtayyeh]] replies that "Netanyahu is the  chief destroyer of the [[Israeli–Palestinian peace process|peace process]]". [https://www.jpost.com/Israel-News/Prime-Minister-Netanyahu-expected-to-announce-annexation-of-Jordan-Valley-601207 (''The Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/netanyahu-seeks-annex-jordan-valley-coordination-u-s-n1051901 (NBC News)]
*[[2019 North Carolina's 9th congressional district special election]]
**In a [[special election]] viewed as prescient to the [[2020 United States elections|2020 elections]], [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Dan Bishop]] beats [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] [[Dan McCready]] by two percentage points. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/09/10/us/politics/north-carolina-special-election.html (''The New York Times'')]
*The [[California State Senate]] approves [[California Assembly Bill 5 (2019)|Assembly Bill 5]], a bill to regulate [[gig economy]] work, introducing a formal test to classify workers as [[independent contractor]]s or [[employee]]s. [https://techcrunch.com/2019/09/10/gig-worker-bill-ab-5-passes-in-california/ (TechCrunch)] [https://theweek.com/speedreads/864127/california-legislators-pass-bill-that-reclassifies-contractors-employees (''The Week'')]
